subject: Feasibility: Combined GLBA + FERPA DPA — KMS / on-prem key custody questions
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pioneertrust.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Adler <ben.adler@pioneertrust.com>, privacy@pioneertrust.com
Date: 2027-10-30T16:12:00Z
Subject: DPA + regulated addenda questions (GLBA + FERPA)

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. PioneerTrust is evaluating Redwood for a new K-12 student lending product that will touch both GLBA-covered consumer financial data and FERPA-covered education records (we own the servicing platform). Our legal and security teams reviewed the standard DPA and have three top-line asks before we can advance to procurement:

1) Key custody: we have to demonstrate customer-managed key control for a subset of PHI/FERPA PII. Is there a vetted KMS/HSM integration (Cloud KMS + external HSM) or an on-prem key-handoff option?

2) Subprocessors: we need a snapshot of all subprocessors that process tokenization, caching, telemetry, and model serving, plus an SLA-driven process for notification and mitigation if a subprocessor changes in-scope.

3) Combined addenda approach: our compliance team would prefer a consolidated addendum that covers GLBA controls (data segregation, logging, encryption at-rest/in-transit, incident timelines) and FERPA-specific requirements (student data handling, minimal access, and auditability). Can Redwood produce a feasibility note and a draft combined addendum?

I attached a short spreadsheet with our team’s specific asks and a sample MAP we typically use for regulated pilots. Can we get a short feasibility summary and a proposed timeline? Ideally we’d have a short call next week with security and product.

Appreciate it —
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Risk
PioneerTrust

Attachments: PioneerTrust_Addendum_Questions.xlsx, MAP_PioneerTrust_Redwood_v1.pdf
From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pioneertrust.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-31T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + regulated addenda questions (GLBA + FERPA)

Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP. Looping in Lauren (legal lead on addenda) and Monica (compliance/solutions) so we can respond with a single feasibility note and proposed next steps.

High level answers up front so your team can decide whether to schedule a deep-dive:

- KMS/key custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations for hosted deployments (we can import keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For stronger custody we offer an HSM-backed option in our Dedicated plan and a private on-prem package that supports local HSMs and key material never leaving your environment. We’ll outline the exact key-wrapping and envelope encryption flow in the feasibility note.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessor snapshot that we update monthly; the snapshot you’ll find attached includes who handles model serving, telemetry, logging, SRE, and third-party monitoring. We can include a contractual notification window (30 days) and an SLA for mitigation steps — need to confirm acceptable windows for you.

- Combined addendum: we can draft a consolidated addendum that merges GLBA-specific language (data segmentation, retention limits, incident reporting aligned to FFIEC practicalities) and FERPA clauses (student-data minimization, audit trails per student id, and teacher/administrator access restrictions). There will be edge cases (for example: how we classify derivative tokens used for caching) that we’ll call out for negotiation.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll produce a short feasibility memo (2–3 pages) addressing KMS options, how data residency can be guaranteed for Dedicated/Private, the subprocessor disclosure, and risk points for a combined addendum.
2) Draft a single consolidated addendum template for PioneerTrust to review.
3) Quick sync (30 min) with your privacy/security and our legal/compliance teams — how does Thursday 11/4 or Friday 11/5 look?

I’ll attach the subprocessor snapshot and a strawman MAP with responsibilities and timeline.

—Connor O’Brien
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: subprocessor_snapshot_2027-10.pdf
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pioneertrust.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Adler <ben.adler@pioneertrust.com>, privacy@pioneertrust.com
Date: 2027-11-01T14:26:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + regulated addenda questions (GLBA + FERPA)

Thanks Connor — that’s helpful. A few clarifying items from our internal team before we lock a call:

- On KMS: can you confirm whether key usage telemetry (e.g., which services requested unwrapping) is visible to PioneerTrust when we use Redwood-managed hardware in Dedicated? We want tamper-evident logs that we can retain for 7 years per our policy.

- On caching: PioneerTrust cannot allow any persistent unencrypted caching of raw student identifiers. Would Redwood’s KV cache and prefix-caching be configurable to only cache tokenized IDs, and can we enforce TTLs at request-level via route policies?

- On on-prem option: what’s the minimum engagement timeline to stand up a private box + on-prem KMS integration? Our infra team prefers a 6-week window for pilot provisioning — is that realistic?

If you can include those specifics in the feasibility memo (especially sample audit log schema and retention options), we’ll confirm availability for a 30-minute call once we review.

OLIVIA

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pioneertrust.com>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-02T16:41:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA + regulated addenda questions (GLBA + FERPA) — Proposed MAP and timeline

Olivia / Ben —

Appreciate the specificity — this is exactly the level of detail we like to see. I’m Lauren (lead counsel for regulated deals). Quick reply with an attached 2‑page feasibility memo and a proposed MAP (both attached in the HubSpot deal). Highlights:

- Key telemetry and logs: For Dedicated + HSM we can provide a KMS access log stream (KeyUsage records) and a signed timeline for retention up to 7 years. Those logs can be pushed to your S3 bucket or to a secure logging endpoint via TLS. We’ll include sample schemas in the memo.

- Caching controls: Redwood runtime supports request-level route policies; we can scope caching to tokenized IDs only and enforce TTLs per route. We’ll add a recommended set of policies for your team.

- On‑prem timeline: 6 weeks is tight but achievable for a pilot if we get provisioning approvals and network access (IP allowlists, peering) within 7 business days of signature. Production rollouts typically take 8–12 weeks.

Next steps proposed (MAP):
1) PioneerTrust to confirm the set of data classes in scope (we’ll provide a simple template).
2) Redwood to deliver draft consolidated addendum + audit log schema (by 11/05).
3) Security deep-dive call (30 min) week of 11/08 — Connor will coordinate with your infra folks.
4) Procurement / redline cycle (2–3 wks) and pilot provisioning start (targeting late Nov).

Please confirm whether you want logs delivered to PioneerTrust S3 or to an endpoint; we’ll prepare a sample onboarding checklist either way.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: MAP_PioneerTrust_Redwood_v1.pdf, PioneerTrust feasibility memo (attached in drive)
